name: memanto
description: Search and question your agents' memory in the sidebar, or let Copilot recall it for you.

commands.name: recall
commands.description: List memories matching what you type

commands.name: remember
commands.description: Save what you type as a memory

disambiguation.description: The user is asking what was previously decided, preferred, agreed or learned on this project, or asking to store something for later.
examples: What did we decide about authentication?
Which database did the team pick, and why?
Remember that we dropped session cookies

languageModelTools.name: memanto_recall
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search what this project's agents have already decided, preferred and learned.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search Memanto, the developer's persistent memory of decisions, preferences, facts, conventions and past mistakes recorded by their coding agents. Call this before answering questions about how this project does things, or before writing code that depends on a past decision (frameworks, APIs, data stores, naming, deployment). Returns memories with type, confidence, provenance and date. Prefer what it returns over assumptions, and say which memory you relied on.

query.description: What to search for, in natural language. For example 'authentication approach' or 'database choice'.

type.description: Optional filter for one memory type.

limit.description: How many memories to return, 1 to 50.

languageModelTools.name: memanto_answer
languageModelTools.userDescription: Ask a question and get an answer written from your stored memories.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Ask Memanto a question and get back a single written answer synthesised from the developer's stored memories, with the memories it used. Use this when the answer needs several memories pulled together, such as why something was decided or how a part of the project came to work the way it does. Prefer memanto_recall when you want the raw memories as evidence, or when you only need to look one thing up: this tool runs a model over the memories, so it is slower and uses the developer's Memanto quota.

question.description: The question to ask, in natural language.

limit.description: How many memories to ground the answer in, 1 to 50.

languageModelTools.name: memanto_remember
languageModelTools.userDescription: Save a decision or fact so this project's other agents can recall it. Asks you first.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Save one durable piece of knowledge to Memanto so the developer's other coding agents can recall it later. Use only for things worth keeping beyond this conversation, such as a decision that was made, a stated preference, or a mistake worth not repeating. Do not use it for transient chat or for restating code. The user is asked to confirm before anything is saved.

content.description: The memory itself, written as one self-contained statement.

type.description: Which kind of memory this is.

memanto.agentId.markdownDescription: Agent whose memories this window uses. Leave empty to follow the active agent in `~/.memanto/config.yaml`.

Connect to a Memanto server you run yourself.
memanto.server.mode.description: Where the extension gets its Memanto server.

memanto.server.startOnStartup.description: Start the private server as soon as the window opens. Off by default: the server starts the first time you use Memanto.

memanto.server.address.markdownDescription: Address of your own server, used when `#memanto.server.mode#` is `attach`. Leave empty to follow `~/.memanto/config.yaml`.

memanto.recallLimit.description: How many memories a recall returns.

memanto.citeOnInsert.description: Add a comment with the type, provenance and date when inserting a memory into a file.

memanto.export.memoriesPerType.description: How many memories of each type an export includes.

walkthroughs.title: Set up Memanto
walkthroughs.description: Install the Memanto CLI and connect this window to your agents' memory.

steps.title: Install Memanto
steps.description:
Memanto is a Python command line tool and needs Python 3.11 or newer.
[Copy install command](command:memanto.setup)

steps.title: Choose a backend
steps.description:
Run `memanto` in a terminal to pick the cloud or on-prem backend and store your key.
[Open setup steps](command:memanto.setup)

steps.title: Open the chat
steps.description:
Search your memories or ask a question. The extension starts the server for you.
[Open chat](command:memanto.openChat)

scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:integration
